About

I'm a trilingual Communications Specialist with over a decade turning scientific and complex content into compelling narratives. My work spans EU-funded research consortia, institutional journalism, podcast and video production, and data-informed content strategy.

From working for a Horizon Europe biotechnology project to expanding media relations for a public research institute across Brazil, I bring a newsroom approach to every brief: accuracy, speed, and storytelling instinct.

Case Study

Case Study: Media Relations

Turning a student's memory into national science news — a press strategy for an archaeological discovery made by a research and education institute project in rural Brazil.

Challenge

A research project with high school students identified prehistoric rock art at a previously unrecorded site. The discovery was relevant, but it came from a rural campus far from major newsrooms.

The goal was to reach national media while keeping the science accurate, by leading with the story behind the discovery.

Strategy
  • A human angle. I built the pitch around the student who made the discovery and how he connected a family memory to what he had learned in class, framing science as part of culture and identity.
  • Close partnership with the researchers. The project team had already started sharing the discovery. When I took over the story, I professionalised and amplified that work. I pitched it through the behind-the-scenes and family-memory angle, prepared the researchers for interviews, and secured space in major outlets.
Results
22
Media stories across TV, radio and online news.
4
National outlets, including a live TV interview.
2
Waves of coverage over more than three months.
Why it worked

The discovery was newsworthy on its own, but the story behind it is what made it spread — from regional outlets to national TV, radio and social media.

A genuine partnership between researchers and communicators was also key. It created a chain of credibility, with the institute as the source, national media as the amplifier and the national heritage authority (Iphan) as the validator.
